correctness.rationale: Three zeros (one real, one conjugate pair) are strictly inside the disk. A direct common-denominator identity gives phase slope 7-2688x^3/((1+9x)(1+2x+49x^2)), whose derivative has strictly negative sign for x>0. The phase difference at frequency 7n equals -6 theta^7+O(theta^9) and has no other stationary point. Rescaled oscillatory integration yields the explicitly positive gamma constant. Uniformly in frequency, dyadic second-derivative van der Corput gives O(n^-1/7) near the sole order-five curvature zero, O(n^-1/3) near the antipode, and O(n^-1/2) elsewhere. For any product of degree m<=2, rational Cayley coordinates limit the order of any nonconstant slope critical flatness to <=2m, yielding uniform O(n^-1/(2m+1))=o(n^-1/7); monomials have constant coefficient supremum 1. Exact polynomial checks and converging finite quadrature are independent numerical corroboration; infinite proof uses analytic inequalities.

Eight actual mathematical-results index searches and targeted public-literature searches revealed no equivalent or dominating statement; identified hits address different Fourier objects. This remains best-knowledge originality, not a claim of comprehensive literature uniqueness.

value.rationale: Borichev–Fouchet–Zarouf explicitly identify the minimum-degree problem and give a degree-four seventh-order witness. Constructing a degree-three witness and proving no one- or two-factor construction possible closes the first unresolved order-seven degree threshold sharply, a structural complexity invariant of the inner function rather than a routine numerical recomputation. The nonzero asymptotic for the exact 7n coefficient identifies its seventh-order stationary phase mechanism. Importance is limited to this order, not asserted for all exponents.
